doc.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Writing lyrics to Weston, Golson and Gryce tunes; Leonard Feather
summary: He lists tunes he wrote words for and explains Leonard Feather wrote Whisper Not.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: All of those guys, you wrote lyrics to their music. Little Niles. Hi-Fly. Doodlin’, which is one of my all-time favorites. Gosh. Who else was there?
I did things for Gigi Gryce and Benny Golson too: Social Call and I Remember Clifford. Stablemates and all those things.
Let’s see. I’m trying to think of the name of this other song. Whisper Not.
Did you write lyrics to Whisper Not?
No. Leonard Feather did, and it was so good I just let it alone, because Leonard’s lyric was great. That was a great lyric. Leonard Feather was an interesting man.
He was. I had the opportunity to meet him once on a panel. I didn’t know that he was a composer.

He composed two of the compositions and supervised Dinah Washington’s first record date. He’s got good bona fides. He’s great. Leonard Feather is a real – he was truly capable of criticizing jazz music, because he could do it.
